questions.stem: Why are comprehensive dilated eye examinations important for people at increased risk for glaucoma?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Glaucoma may have no early symptoms, and a comprehensive dilated eye examination can detect disease before additional irreversible vision loss occurs.","B":"Glaucoma reliably produces severe eye pain before optic-nerve damage, so examination is unnecessary in an asymptomatic high-risk person.","C":"A routine blood test detects glaucoma earlier than an eye examination and is the preferred test for people at increased risk.","D":"Glaucoma develops only after severe central vision loss is present, so examination before visual symptoms has little value."}}
questions.rationale: NEI states that glaucoma can be asymptomatic early and that people at increased risk are best evaluated with comprehensive dilated eye examinations; early detection and treatment can help prevent further vision loss.

questions.stem: A client spends several hours each day performing repetitive handwashing rituals in response to intrusive contamination fears and has marked distress when unable to complete them. Which condition is most consistent with this pattern?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Social anxiety disorder, in which the core fear is scrutiny or embarrassment rather than contamination obsessions with washing rituals.","B":"Body dysmorphic disorder, in which the central preoccupation is perceived appearance defects rather than contamination fears.","C":"Obsessive-compulsive disorder, in which intrusive contamination obsessions can drive time-consuming cleaning or handwashing compulsions.","D":"Generalized anxiety disorder, in which broad excessive worry occurs without repetitive compulsions performed in response to obsessions."}}
questions.rationale: NIMH describes OCD as involving obsessions and compulsions; excessive cleaning or handwashing is a common compulsion, and clinically significant symptoms are time-consuming or cause distress/interference.

questions.stem: A client is preoccupied with a slight or unnoticeable perceived flaw in appearance, repeatedly checks mirrors and seeks reassurance, and has substantial social impairment. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Obsessive-compulsive disorder, when obsessions and compulsions are present but are not centered on perceived appearance defects.","B":"Social anxiety disorder, when fear of scrutiny or embarrassment is primary without a persistent perceived appearance flaw.","C":"Illness anxiety disorder, when fear of having or acquiring serious disease is primary rather than perceived appearance defects.","D":"Body dysmorphic disorder, characterized by preoccupation with slight or unobservable appearance flaws plus repetitive appearance-related behaviors."}}
questions.rationale: Body dysmorphic disorder involves preoccupation with perceived defects that are not observable or appear slight to others, repetitive appearance-related behaviors such as mirror checking/reassurance seeking, and clinically significant distress or impairment.
